disposition_reason: Forty chocolate bars made in Brazil (five brands each of 40%, 50%, 60% and 70% cocoa, milk, white, sugar-free milk and sugar-free white) bought in Natal were analysed for total arsenic by the silver diethyldithiocarbamate spectrophotometric method; Table 2 prints a value per bar.

study.design: retail survey, 8 chocolate types x 5 brands
study.origin: produced in Brazil (national and international brands)
study.market: commercial establishments in Natal, Rio Grande do Norte, Brazil
study.method: dry ashing with MgO/Mg(NO3)2, arsine generation with Zn/KI, silver diethyldithiocarbamate spectrophotometry; 2.5 g sample
study.lod_text: not determined in the study; cites LQ of 0.1-0.2 µg/g for the method from the literature
study.qa: duplicate determinations, daily calibration curves (R2 0.9963-1.0); no CRM or spike recovery performed (literature recoveries 85-102% cited)

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Brazil Anvisa RDC 42/2013 and IN 160/2022 maximum arsenic level in chocolate

unresolved: Total arsenic only; no inorganic arsenic speciation.
White chocolate results do not follow the printed calibration curve (see integrity_flag); the curve equation for white chocolate may be misprinted.
Sugar-free white chocolate bar 3 has a printed manufacturing date of 09/2025, after the stated collection period (April 2024 to May 2025).
The method's detection and quantification limits were not determined in-house; several values (0.029-0.083 µg/g) are below the cited quantification range.
